sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan. Draft circulated for discussion, Cambridge, 10 January 2021, 25 pp. (via web.archive.org copy of rogerblench.info)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Kendeje. Kendeje appears only in Table 1 (name, location, 1,860 speakers, dialects Yaali/Faranga) and the tree; sec. 2.3 states 'Our only knowledge of some varieties appears to be from SIL Survey reports, mostly unpublished, and not always including the data on which the conclusions are based (e.g. Maass, Grant & Prinz 1995, 1996..)'. Sec. 4.3 'Tones' covers Maba (H, L, R, F per Weiss 2009) and Aiki (two heights) only; no stress discussion; comparative wordlist (Table 13, from Edgar 1991b) has no Kendeje column.

sources.citation: Weiss, Doris. 2009. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du maba. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2. 461 pp. (HAL tel-01540280)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes MABA (maba1277), the closest documented relative, not Kendeje; the word 'kendeje/kendedje/yaali/faranga' does not occur in the thesis. For Maba, sec. 2.2.1 'Accent tonique' (pp. 43-45): intensity accent is non-distinctive and predictable from tone height (every H syllable stressed), vowel length (long vowels stressed) and word shape; tone is distinctive. Not usable as a Kendeje statement.

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Angela Prinz & Caroline Grant. 1996. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: première évaluation parmi les Kendedje du Ouaddaï. N'Djaména: Association SIL. ii+12 pp. (SIL archive 50809; downloaded via web.archive.org snapshot of the sil.org PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic first-assessment survey (fieldwork 26-27 Jan 1995): classification by lexicostatistics (Kendeje 69-71% with Maba, 59-64% with Masalit), bilingualism, vitality. No phonology; wordlists collected but not printed (only the similarity table, App. B). States (sec. 1.2) that Kendeje was until then 'un parler jusqu'à présent inconnu au monde académique'.

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Caroline Grant & Angela Prinz. 1995-1996. Unpublished Kendeje-Yaali and Kendeje-Faranga survey wordlists (WordSurv database) underlying the 1996 Rapport d'enquête; Association SIL Tchad archives, N'Djaména.
